payload.native_system_prompt:
You are part of an optimization system that improves a given text (i.e. the variable). You are the gradient (feedback) engine. Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. The variables may be solutions to problems, prompts to language models, code, or any other text-based variable. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. Your only job is to send feedback and criticism (compute 'gradients'). For instance, feedback can be in the form of 'Since language models have the X failure mode...', 'Adding X can fix this error because...', 'Removing X can improve the objective function because...', 'Changing X to Y would fix the mistake ...', that gets at the downstream objective.
If a variable is already working well (e.g. the objective function is perfect, an evaluation shows the response is accurate), you should not give feedback.

### Glossary of tags that will be sent to you:
# - <LM_SYSTEM_PROMPT>: The system prompt for the language model.
# - <LM_INPUT>: The input to the language model.
# - <LM_OUTPUT>: The output of the language model.
# - <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION>: The objective of the optimization task.
# - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.
# - <ROLE>: The role description of the variable.
payload.instruction: Move the book behind the flower
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Does the edited image show clear progress toward placing the book behind a flower, even if the requested relation is not complete?
node.criteria: Pass only if comparison with the source shows visible movement of the book toward a behind-flower relation, or other clear relational progress. Fail only if the book and relevant flower are identifiable and evidence shows no such progress, including a clearly unchanged or still-separated relation. Unknown if identity, comparison, or progress cannot be determined. Appearance changes or proximity alone are not progress; a completed relation is not a failure for lack of further movement.
node.binding: Compare source and edited images for the book's relative placement and depth with respect to a flower. Judge movement toward the requested relation, not merely object appearance or proximity. Do not require matching the exact source rose when the edited flower identity is ambiguous; preserve unknown if the relevant relation or progress cannot be assessed.

node_traces.evidence: The book has been moved from its original position and is now close to a flower, showing relational progress toward placing it behind one. The edited image does not clearly establish that the book is actually behind the flower.

The edited image shows the book moved into the area beside the flowers, with its blue cover partly behind the open book and near the flowers. This is visible relational progress compared with the source, where the book and rose are clearly separated, though the requested behind-flower relation is not clearly complete.

The book has been moved from its original position toward the flowers and now overlaps the nearer flower in the image, showing clear relational progress toward placing it behind a flower. The depth relation is not clearly complete.

The book has been moved from its original position toward the flowers and now overlaps the nearer flower in the image, showing clear relational progress toward placing it behind a flower. The depth ordering is not clearly complete, but this check asks only for progress.

fulfillment: The node’s completion criterion is appropriately strict, but its progress signal is over-crediting proximity or movement toward the target. In the edited image, the blue book is near the flowers, yet neither flower visibly occludes it; the book appears behind the open book, not behind a flower. The source shows the book and rose separated, but the edit also changes the scene substantially (including the flowers’ appearance/count and the open book), so do not infer requested progress merely from a changed position or closeness. Tighten s2’s binding to require evidence that the requested book–flower relation itself has advanced relative to the source, and distinguish that from unrelated edits or adjacency; if evidence is ambiguous, preserve unknown rather than pass. Keep s1 focused on completed depth ordering and retain the existing rule that absence requires affirmative evidence of no progress. The repeated high-confidence partial outputs indicate a systematic criterion/binding issue, not transport or dependency failure: all checks are valid, queried, and have no execution failures. Do not force the reference label; use it as an aggregate diagnostic while grounding decisions in visible evidence.
